1	---
2	tags: [architecture, people-hub, directus]
3	---
4	
5	## People hub: schema and permission model
6	
7	Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
8	hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
9	deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.
10	
11	### Scope and non-goals
12	
13	- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
14	  the camp schedule (programs/sessions/classes/capacity), and registrations. No household
15	  grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household, only per-registration guardians and emergency
16	  contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
17	- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
18	  (`CampSession`), **class** (`CampClass`), **registration** (`Registration`/`RegistrationCampSession`)
19	  — not "enrollment."
20	- Registration status and person contact fields get **history, not just a current value** — see
21	  [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance).
22	- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
23	  below.
24	- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
25	  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.
26	
27	### Collections
28	
29	**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
30	contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
31	Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
32	participant from a `registrations` row.
33	
34	No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
35	contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
36	and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
37	problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.
38	
39	| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
40	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
41	| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
42	| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
43	| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
44	| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
45	| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |
46	
47	**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
48	can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
49	contact).
50	
51	| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
52	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
53	| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
54	| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
55	| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |
56	
57	**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
58	emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
59	relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
60	one's `relationship_type` enum.
61	
62	Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
63	guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
64	(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
65	is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
66	fields into rows here.
67	
68	| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
69	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
70	| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
71	| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
72	| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
73	| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
74	| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |
75	
76	**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
77	(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
78	[Permission model](#permission-model).
79

irrelevant for a session where `sessions.all_classes` is true (every program class applies). No

input.new_string:
**session_classes** — which classes a session actually offers, i.e. the camp schedule itself. A
pure join, no fields of its own. Denormalized: Clubspot represents this as either an explicit
`CampSession.campClassesArray` or an `allClasses` flag meaning "every class in the program" — #70's
sync expands the `allClasses` case into one row per program class at sync time, so this table always
holds the actual explicit list and nothing downstream needs to special-case the flag. No Clubspot id
of its own — it's an array (or a flag) on `CampSession`, not a separate object — so #70 just
reconciles rows to match Clubspot's current state each sync (remove rows no longer present, add new
ones).

1	---
2	tags: [architecture, people-hub, directus]
3	---
4	
5	## People hub: schema and permission model
6	
7	Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
8	hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
9	deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.
10	
11	### Scope and non-goals
12	
13	- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
14	  the camp schedule (programs/sessions/classes/capacity), and registrations. No household
15	  grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household, only per-registration guardians and emergency
16	  contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
17	- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
18	  (`CampSession`), **class** (`CampClass`), **registration** (`Registration`/`RegistrationCampSession`)
19	  — not "enrollment."
20	- Registration status and person contact fields get **history, not just a current value** — see
21	  [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance).
22	- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
23	  below.
24	- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
25	  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.
26	
27	### Collections
28	
29	**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
30	contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
31	Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
32	participant from a `registrations` row.
33	
34	No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
35	contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
36	and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
37	problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.
38	
39	| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
40	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
41	| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
42	| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
43	| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
44	| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
45	| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |
46	
47	**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
48	can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
49	contact).
50	
51	| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
52	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
53	| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
54	| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
55	| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |
56	
57	**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
58	emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
59	relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
60	one's `relationship_type` enum.
61	
62	Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
63	guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
64	(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
65	is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
66	fields into rows here.
67	
68	| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
69	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
70	| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
71	| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
72	| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
73	| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
74	| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |
75	
76	**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
77	(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
78	[Permission model](#permission-model).
79	
80	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
81	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
82	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
83	| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
84	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
85	
86	**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
87	(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.
88	
89	| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                                                          |
90	| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
91	| `id`               | uuid                     | primary key                                                                    |
92	| `name`             | string                   |                                                                                |
93	| `category`         | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
94	| `clubspot_camp_id` | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                                                              |
95	
96	**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).
97	
98	| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
99	| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
100	| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
101	| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
102	| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
103	| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |
104	
105	**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
106	"Advanced"). A registration is for a specific session _and_ class — see `registrations` below.
107	
108	| Field               | Type                      | Notes                                                                  |
109	| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
110	| `id`                | uuid                      | primary key                                                            |
111	| `program_id`        | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
112	| `name`              | string                    |                                                                        |
113	| `clubspot_class_id` | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70                                                      |
114	
115	**session_classes** — which classes a session actually offers, i.e. the camp schedule itself. A
116	pure join, no fields of its own. Denormalized: Clubspot represents this as either an explicit
117	`CampSession.campClassesArray` or an `allClasses` flag meaning "every class in the program" — #70's
118	sync expands the `allClasses` case into one row per program class at sync time, so this table always
119	holds the actual explicit list and nothing downstream needs to special-case the flag. No Clubspot id
120	of its own — it's an array (or a flag) on `CampSession`, not a separate object — so #70 just
121	reconciles rows to match Clubspot's current state each sync (remove rows no longer present, add new
122	ones).
123	
124	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
125	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
126	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
127	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
128	| `class_id`   | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`  |             |
129	
130	**entry_caps** — capacity, matching Clubspot's `EntryCap` exactly: a cap on one class, either
131	overall (`session_id` null, applies across every session) or for one specific session.
132	
133	| Field                   | Type                                | Notes                                            |
134	| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
135	| `id`                    | uuid                                | primary key                                      |
136	| `class_id`              | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`            |                                                  |
137	| `session_id`            | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`, nullable | null = applies to this class across all sessions |
138	| `cap`                   | integer                             | the actual limit (Clubspot's own field name)     |
139	| `clubspot_entry_cap_id` | string, nullable, unique            | dedup key for #70                                |
140	
141	This — `programs` / `sessions` / `classes` / `session_classes` / `entry_caps` — is the camp
142	schedule: worth capturing accurately from #70's first sync rather than backfilling later, since the
143	website and the eventual financial-model app both need it, not just rosters/permissions.
144	
145	**registrations** — a participant's registration for one session + class (Clubspot's own term —
146	matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is deliberately at Clubspot's finest grain, its
147	`RegistrationCampSession` join ("Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`) rather than
148	its parent `Registration` object: a single Clubspot registration spanning multiple weeks/classes
149	becomes multiple rows here, one per session+class, matching what the current spreadsheet already
150	does. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out of scope, same as the rest of
151	the financial model.
152	
153	| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                                                                                                                            |
154	| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
155	| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key                                                                                                                      |
156	| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant                                                                                                                  |
157	| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                                                                                                  |
158	| `class_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                                                                                                  |
159	| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the _current_ status — see [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance) for history |
160	| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable                            | groups rows from the same parent Clubspot registration (a multi-session signup); **not unique alone**                            |
161	| `clubspot_session_join_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | the true per-row dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id)                                                          |
162	
163	### Change tracking and provenance
164	
165	Directus already does this: every API-driven create/update/delete is logged in `directus_activity`
166	(who, when, on what) with a paired `directus_revisions` row holding the full item snapshot and a
167	delta — for every collection, no opt-in needed. Architecture.md already assumed this
168	(`Audit — Directus activity log for data access/changes`), so there's no need for bespoke history
169	tables here, as long as #70 always writes through the Directus API (never raw SQL):
170	
171	- **Registration status** (waitlist → confirmed → cancelled) doesn't need its own event log — the
172	  revision history on a `registrations` row already shows every state it's been in and when Directus
173	  recorded each change. If Clubspot's own historical timestamps
174	  (`RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates`) matter and not just "when we noticed," #70's first
175	  import of a registration can replay each transition as its own sequential write so the revision
176	  _order_ matches reality — though the revision _timestamp_ is always "when Directus saw the write,"
177	  not the original Clubspot moment; a backfill can't inject history at an arbitrary past time.
178	- **Person contact-field changes** (a guardian's email changing between registrations two years
179	  apart) are the same story: the revision history on a `people` row already shows every value
180	  `email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` has held. Confirmed by looking at the live participants
181	  spreadsheet (the thing #70/#95 replace) — it's a fully-rebuilt-every-run flat snapshot with no
182	  timestamp or version on any row today, which is the actual gap here, and Directus's activity log
183	  closes it without any schema of our own.
184	
185	**What the activity log doesn't give us:** a revision is attributed to the Directus user who made
186	the write — for #70's automated updates that's always the sync's own service account, not _which
187	registration_ supplied a given value. No dedicated pointer for that here: `registrations.person_id`
188	already gives every registration a person touched, so "which one most recently supplied this email"
189	is a join against that plus the revision timestamps, not a separate FK on `people`.
190	
191	### Auth identity
192	
193	Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
194	— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
195	Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:
196

tags: [architecture, people-hub, directus]
---

## People hub: schema and permission model

Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.

### Scope and non-goals

- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
  the camp schedule (programs/sessions/classes/capacity), and registrations. No household
  grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household, only per-registration guardians and emergency
  contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
  (`CampSession`), **class** (`CampClass`), **registration** (`Registration`/`RegistrationCampSession`)
  — not "enrollment."
- Registration status and person contact fields get **history, not just a current value** — see
  [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance).
- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
  below.
- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.

### Collections

**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
participant from a `registrations` row.

No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.

| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |

**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
contact).

| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |

**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
one's `relationship_type` enum.

Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
fields into rows here.

| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |

**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
[Permission model](#permission-model).

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |

**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.

| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`               | uuid                     | primary key                                                                    |
| `name`             | string                   |                                                                                |
| `category`         | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
| `clubspot_camp_id` | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                                                              |

**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).

| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |

**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
"Advanced"). A registration is for a specific session _and_ class — see `registrations` below.

| Field               | Type                      | Notes                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | uuid                      | primary key                                                            |
| `program_id`        | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
| `name`              | string                    |                                                                        |
| `clubspot_class_id` | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70                                                      |

**session_classes** — which classes a session actually offers, i.e. the camp schedule itself. A
pure join, no fields of its own. Denormalized: Clubspot represents this as either an explicit
`CampSession.campClassesArray` or an `allClasses` flag meaning "every class in the program" — #70's
sync expands the `allClasses` case into one row per program class at sync time, so this table always
holds the actual explicit list and nothing downstream needs to special-case the flag. No Clubspot id
of its own — it's an array (or a flag) on `CampSession`, not a separate object — so #70 just
reconciles rows to match Clubspot's current state each sync (remove rows no longer present, add new
ones).

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
| `class_id`   | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`  |             |

**entry_caps** — capacity, matching Clubspot's `EntryCap` exactly: a cap on one class, either
overall (`session_id` null, applies across every session) or for one specific session.

| Field                   | Type                                | Notes                                            |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`                    | uuid                                | primary key                                      |
| `class_id`              | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`            |                                                  |
| `session_id`            | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`, nullable | null = applies to this class across all sessions |
| `cap`                   | integer                             | the actual limit (Clubspot's own field name)     |
| `clubspot_entry_cap_id` | string, nullable, unique            | dedup key for #70                                |

This — `programs` / `sessions` / `classes` / `session_classes` / `entry_caps` — is the camp
schedule: worth capturing accurately from #70's first sync rather than backfilling later, since the
website and the eventual financial-model app both need it, not just rosters/permissions.

**registrations** — a participant's registration for one session + class (Clubspot's own term —
matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is deliberately at Clubspot's finest grain, its
`RegistrationCampSession` join ("Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`) rather than
its parent `Registration` object: a single Clubspot registration spanning multiple weeks/classes
becomes multiple rows here, one per session+class, matching what the current spreadsheet already
does. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out of scope, same as the rest of
the financial model.

| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key                                                                                                                      |
| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant                                                                                                                  |
| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                                                                                                  |
| `class_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                                                                                                  |
| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the _current_ status — see [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance) for history |
| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable                            | groups rows from the same parent Clubspot registration (a multi-session signup); **not unique alone**                            |
| `clubspot_session_join_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | the true per-row dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id)                                                          |

### Change tracking and provenance

Directus already does this: every API-driven create/update/delete is logged in `directus_activity`
(who, when, on what) with a paired `directus_revisions` row holding the full item snapshot and a
delta — for every collection, no opt-in needed. Architecture.md already assumed this
(`Audit — Directus activity log for data access/changes`), so there's no need for bespoke history
tables here, as long as #70 always writes through the Directus API (never raw SQL):

- **Registration status** (waitlist → confirmed → cancelled) doesn't need its own event log — the
  revision history on a `registrations` row already shows every state it's been in and when Directus
  recorded each change. If Clubspot's own historical timestamps
  (`RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates`) matter and not just "when we noticed," #70's first
  import of a registration can replay each transition as its own sequential write so the revision
  _order_ matches reality — though the revision _timestamp_ is always "when Directus saw the write,"
  not the original Clubspot moment; a backfill can't inject history at an arbitrary past time.
- **Person contact-field changes** (a guardian's email changing between registrations two years
  apart) are the same story: the revision history on a `people` row already shows every value
  `email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` has held. Confirmed by looking at the live participants
  spreadsheet (the thing #70/#95 replace) — it's a fully-rebuilt-every-run flat snapshot with no
  timestamp or version on any row today, which is the actual gap here, and Directus's activity log
  closes it without any schema of our own.

**What the activity log doesn't give us:** a revision is attributed to the Directus user who made
the write — for #70's automated updates that's always the sync's own service account, not _which
registration_ supplied a given value. No dedicated pointer for that here: `registrations.person_id`
already gives every registration a person touched, so "which one most recently supplied this email"
is a join against that plus the revision timestamps, not a separate FK on `people`.

### Auth identity

Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:

- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
  at the resulting user once one exists.

### Permission model

- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
  (needs #65). KISS for now: any authenticated Directus user can read `sessions` / `registrations` /
  `people` roster fields (no `medical_profiles`) — scoping a coach to only their own sessions via
  `event_staff` is a follow-up, not built here.
- **Guardian** — same login caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` /
  `medical_profiles` / `registrations`, filtered through `contacts` where
  `relationship_type == 'guardian'`. This scoping isn't KISS'd away like the coach roster case above
  — it's the medical-data boundary the whole design doc exists to get right.
- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
  record (`contacts` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal audience.

### Open questions for the applying slice (#95)

- Exact Directus field types (`uuid` vs. Directus's integer PKs) for every collection above — pick
  whichever keeps the permission filters simplest when building the real schema snapshot.
- Whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level (not just collection-level) permissions before a
  Guardian role ever actually logs in.
- The actual person-dedup rule #70 will use (email match, most likely, with a manual merge path for
  the rest) — out of scope here, but the schema above assumes one exists.
- Whether contact-field provenance ever needs more than "join `registrations` on `person_id` and
  compare revision timestamps" — not built now; revisit if that join turns out too awkward for staff
  to actually use.

5	## People hub: schema and permission model
6	
7	Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
8	hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
9	deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.
10	
11	### Scope and non-goals
12	
13	- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
14	  the camp schedule (programs/sessions/classes/capacity), and registrations. No household
15	  grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household, only per-registration guardians and emergency
16	  contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
17	- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
18	  (`CampSession`), **class** (`CampClass`), **registration** (`Registration`/`RegistrationCampSession`)
19	  — not "enrollment."
20	- Registration status and person contact fields get **history, not just a current value** — see
21	  [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance).
22	- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
23	  below.
24	- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
25	  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.
26	
27	### Collections
28	
29	**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
30	contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
31	Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
32	participant from a `registrations` row (see [Collections](#collections) below).
33	
34	No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
35	contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
36	and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
37	problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.
38	
39	| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
40	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
41	| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
42	| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
43	| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
44	| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
45	| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |
46	
47	**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
48	can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
49	contact).
50	
51	| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
52	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
53	| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
54	| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
55	| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |
56	
57	**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
58	emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
59	relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
60	one's `relationship_type` enum.
61	
62	Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
63	guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
64	(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
65	is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
66	fields into rows here.
67	
68	| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
69	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
70	| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
71	| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
72	| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
73	| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
74	| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |
75	
76	**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
77	(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
78	[Permission model](#permission-model).
79	
80	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
81	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
82	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
83	| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
84	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
85	
86	**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
87	(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.
88	
89	| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                                                          |
90	| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
91	| `id`               | uuid                     | primary key                                                                    |
92	| `name`             | string                   |                                                                                |
93	| `category`         | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
94	| `clubspot_camp_id` | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                                                              |
95	
96	**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).
97	
98	| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
99	| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
100	| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
101	| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
102	| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
103	| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |
104	
105	**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.

107	`registration_entries` below.

input.description: Inspect portal Caddyfile and Dockerfile

content.thinking:
I see now that the Caddyfile is baked into the portal's Docker image at build time, tied to a single host block for the site domain. To support a second hostname for Directus with its own reverse proxy and different auth mechanism, I'll need to modify the Caddy config to handle multiple host blocks with distinct upstreams.

I'm weighing whether to add both site blocks into the same shared Caddyfile within the portal's image (since the compose stack already runs one shared Caddy instance, matching earlier design decisions to route by hostname) versus creating a separate dedicated reverse-proxy service instead.

# The cycsail.team portal compose stack, run on the substrate VM.
#
# Two containers: our Caddy image (baked with the static site) fronting oauth2-proxy (Google auth,
# restricted to the all@ group). Secret values come from an env file written at boot from Secret
# Manager (see cloud-init in infrastructure/src/compute.ts) — nothing sensitive lives in git.
services:
  caddy:
    image: ${PORTAL_IMAGE}
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      SITE_DOMAIN: ${SITE_DOMAIN}
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    depends_on:
      - oauth2-proxy

  oauth2-proxy:
    image: quay.io/oauth2-proxy/oauth2-proxy:v7.6.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    command:
      - --http-address=0.0.0.0:4180
      - --reverse-proxy=true
      # Auth-only in front of Caddy: oauth2-proxy makes the allow/deny decision; Caddy serves.
      - --upstream=static://202
      - --provider=google
      - --redirect-url=https://${SITE_DOMAIN}/oauth2/callback
      - --cookie-domain=${SITE_DOMAIN}
      - --whitelist-domain=${SITE_DOMAIN}
      # Accept any Google account (personal Gmail included); the group check below is the real gate.
      - --email-domain=*
      # Authorization = membership in the all@ group (which nests staff@, volunteers@, …).
      - --google-group=${OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_GROUP}
      - --google-admin-email=${OAUTH2_PROXY_GOOGLE_ADMIN_EMAIL}
      # Use the VM's own service account (Application Default Credentials via the metadata server)
      # for the Directory API group lookup — no long-lived key file. The substrate SA must have
      # domain-wide delegation for admin.directory.group.readonly (see ../README.md).
      - --google-use-application-default-credentials=true
      - --set-xauthrequest=true
    environment:
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID: ${OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_ID}
      OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_SECRET: ${OAUTH2_PROXY_CLIENT_SECRET}
      OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET: ${OAUTH2_PROXY_COOKIE_SECRET}

volumes:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

content.thinking:
The preview looks clean: 6 secrets, 6 grants, the DNS record, and the database are all set to be created with no errors. The metadata diff on the substrate compute instance is expected since my bootstrap changes will legitimately update the VM's user-data — that's the intended effect of this change, not leftover drift.

The two reauth errors are the same pre-existing, unrelated OAuth token freshness issue for the docker registry builds — nothing I need to address.

With the Pulumi-level additions confirmed sound, I'm moving to the bigger remaining piece: the schema-apply work, building a Directus schema snapshot plus roles/policies matching the people-hub schema docs, along with the manual-setup documentation. Given how important it is to get an authoritative schema, I want to spin up a real local Directus and Postgres via podman to author and validate the schema, then export an actual snapshot file to commit — starting with an ephemeral postgres container on a distinct port, followed by a local Directus instance pointed at it.

I need Directus to bootstrap with known admin credentials via env vars, then use its API or CLI to build out the collections, fields, relations, roles, and policies from the schema doc, export the result with a schema snapshot command into a committed file, and finally tear down the temporary containers so nothing stray is left behind. Realizing this is a lot of manual API work to properly construct roughly nine collections with correct field types, foreign keys, relations, and permissions, I'm weighing whether this level of effort fits within the scope of one turn.

Since this would take dozens of individual API calls, I think the better approach is to commit the current infra generalization work now as a checkpoint, then continue with the schema-authoring work as a subsequent commit within the same PR, since the ask was to combine these pieces into one PR rather than split them across multiple.

content.thinking:
Now I'm turning to the schema authoring work, the biggest remaining piece. I'm planning to spin up a temporary local Postgres and Directus instance via podman with dedicated container names to avoid collisions, so I can build out the schema and export a snapshot from it.

I'd need to check available ports, wait for the containers to become healthy, then authenticate and use the REST API to create collections, fields, and relations matching the design doc, plus set up roles and policies for Administrator/Staff/Coach/Guardian. After that I'd generate a schema snapshot via the Directus CLI and tear everything down. Given the complexity and time this API-driven approach would take, I'm reconsidering a lighter path: hand-authoring the schema snapshot YAML directly based on what I know of Directus's schema format.

Hand-authoring risks subtle format errors since Directus validates snapshots strictly on apply, but doing it live via API guarantees validity at the cost of setup time and many calls. Since the verification note implies live testing is preferred when feasible, and it looks feasible here, I'll go with the live approach for a genuinely verified artifact -- starting by checking for port conflicts before setup.

content.content:
1	---
2	tags: [architecture, people-hub, directus]
3	---
4	
5	## People hub: schema and permission model
6	
7	Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
8	hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
9	deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.
10	
11	### Scope and non-goals
12	
13	- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
14	  the camp schedule (programs/sessions/classes/capacity), and registrations. No household
15	  grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household, only per-registration guardians and emergency
16	  contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
17	- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
18	  (`CampSession`), **class** (`CampClass`), **registration** (`Registration`/`RegistrationCampSession`)
19	  — not "enrollment."
20	- Registration status and person contact fields get **history, not just a current value** — see
21	  [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance).
22	- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
23	  below.
24	- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
25	  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.
26	
27	### Collections
28	
29	**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
30	contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
31	Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
32	participant from a `registrations` row (see [Collections](#collections) below).
33	
34	No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
35	contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
36	and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
37	problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.
38	
39	| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
40	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
41	| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
42	| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
43	| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
44	| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
45	| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |
46	
47	**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
48	can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
49	contact).
50	
51	| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
52	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
53	| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
54	| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
55	| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |
56	
57	**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
58	emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
59	relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
60	one's `relationship_type` enum.
61	
62	Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
63	guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
64	(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
65	is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
66	fields into rows here.
67	
68	| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
69	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
70	| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
71	| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
72	| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
73	| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
74	| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |
75	
76	**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
77	(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
78	[Permission model](#permission-model).
79	
80	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
81	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
82	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
83	| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
84	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
85	
86	**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
87	(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.
88	
89	| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                                                          |
90	| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
91	| `id`               | uuid                     | primary key                                                                    |
92	| `name`             | string                   |                                                                                |
93	| `category`         | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
94	| `clubspot_camp_id` | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                                                              |
95	
96	**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).
97	
98	| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
99	| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
100	| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
101	| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
102	| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
103	| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |
104	
105	**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.

## People hub: schema and permission model

Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.

### Scope and non-goals

- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
  the camp schedule (programs/sessions/classes/capacity), and registrations. No household
  grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household, only per-registration guardians and emergency
  contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
  (`CampSession`), **class** (`CampClass`), **registration** (`Registration`/`RegistrationCampSession`)
  — not "enrollment."
- Registration status and person contact fields get **history, not just a current value** — see
  [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance).
- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
  below.
- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.

### Collections

**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
participant from a `registrations` row (see [Collections](#collections) below).

No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.

| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |

**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
contact).

| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |

**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
one's `relationship_type` enum.

Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
fields into rows here.

| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |

**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
[Permission model](#permission-model).

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |

**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.

| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`               | uuid                     | primary key                                                                    |
| `name`             | string                   |                                                                                |
| `category`         | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
| `clubspot_camp_id` | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                                                              |

**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).

| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |

**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
"Advanced"). Each registration entry is for a specific session _and_ class — see
`registration_entries` below.

| Field               | Type                      | Notes                                                                  |
| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | uuid                      | primary key                                                            |
| `program_id`        | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
| `name`              | string                    |                                                                        |
| `clubspot_class_id` | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70                                                      |

**session_classes** — which classes a session actually offers, i.e. the camp schedule itself. A
pure join, no fields of its own. Denormalized: Clubspot represents this as either an explicit
`CampSession.campClassesArray` or an `allClasses` flag meaning "every class in the program" — #70's
sync expands the `allClasses` case into one row per program class at sync time, so this table always
holds the actual explicit list and nothing downstream needs to special-case the flag. No Clubspot id
of its own — it's an array (or a flag) on `CampSession`, not a separate object — so #70 just
reconciles rows to match Clubspot's current state each sync (remove rows no longer present, add new
ones).

| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
| `class_id`   | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`  |             |

**entry_caps** — capacity, matching Clubspot's `EntryCap` exactly: a cap on one class, either
overall (`session_id` null, applies across every session) or for one specific session.

| Field                   | Type                                | Notes                                            |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`                    | uuid                                | primary key                                      |
| `class_id`              | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`            |                                                  |
| `session_id`            | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`, nullable | null = applies to this class across all sessions |
| `cap`                   | integer                             | the actual limit (Clubspot's own field name)     |
| `clubspot_entry_cap_id` | string, nullable, unique            | dedup key for #70                                |

This — `programs` / `sessions` / `classes` / `session_classes` / `entry_caps` — is the camp
schedule: worth capturing accurately from #70's first sync rather than backfilling later, since the
website and the eventual financial-model app both need it, not just rosters/permissions.

**registrations** — one row per Clubspot `Registration` object: a participant's signup for a
program (Clubspot's own term — matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is the parent; a single
registration can cover multiple sessions/classes (a multi-week camp signup), which is what
`registration_entries` below is for. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out
of scope, same as the rest of the financial model.

| Field                      | Type                      | Notes             |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `id`                       | uuid                      | primary key       |
| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   | the participant   |
| `program_id`               | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |

**registration_entries** — one row per session + class within a registration (Clubspot's
`RegistrationCampSession` — "Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`). A registration
spanning multiple weeks/classes becomes multiple entries here, matching what the current spreadsheet
already does.

| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key                                                                                                                      |
| `registration_id`          | uuid, FK -> `registrations.id`              |                                                                                                                                  |
| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                                                                                                  |
| `class_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                                                                                                  |
| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the _current_ status — see [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance) for history |
| `clubspot_session_join_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id)                                                                           |

### Change tracking and provenance

Directus already does this: every API-driven create/update/delete is logged in `directus_activity`
(who, when, on what) with a paired `directus_revisions` row holding the full item snapshot and a
delta — for every collection, no opt-in needed. Architecture.md already assumed this
(`Audit — Directus activity log for data access/changes`), so there's no need for bespoke history
tables here, as long as #70 always writes through the Directus API (never raw SQL):

- **Registration status** (waitlist → confirmed → cancelled) doesn't need its own event log — the
  revision history on a `registration_entries` row already shows every state it's been in and when
  Directus recorded each change. If Clubspot's own historical timestamps
  (`RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates`) matter and not just "when we noticed," #70's first
  import of a registration can replay each transition as its own sequential write so the revision
  _order_ matches reality — though the revision _timestamp_ is always "when Directus saw the write,"
  not the original Clubspot moment; a backfill can't inject history at an arbitrary past time.
- **Person contact-field changes** (a guardian's email changing between registrations two years
  apart) are the same story: the revision history on a `people` row already shows every value
  `email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` has held. Confirmed by looking at the live participants
  spreadsheet (the thing #70/#95 replace) — it's a fully-rebuilt-every-run flat snapshot with no
  timestamp or version on any row today, which is the actual gap here, and Directus's activity log
  closes it without any schema of our own.

**What the activity log doesn't give us:** a revision is attributed to the Directus user who made
the write — for #70's automated updates that's always the sync's own service account, not _which
registration_ supplied a given value. No dedicated pointer for that here: `registrations.person_id`
already gives every registration a person touched, so "which one most recently supplied this email"
is a join against that plus the revision timestamps, not a separate FK on `people`.

### Auth identity

Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:

- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
  at the resulting user once one exists.

### Permission model

- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including

- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet

  `registration_entries` / `people` roster fields (no `medical_profiles`) — scoping a coach to only

- **Guardian** — same login caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` /
